title: Attention-based addressee selection for service and social robots to interact with multiple persons

fields.value: Technical/system description with real-world field experiments.

quotes.text: This paper presents two new approaches of attention-based addressee selection for social robots to interact with multiple persons.
We have conducted on-site experiments with a robot receptionist in various interaction scenarios.
The two methods have been implemented in A-Star prototype robots and have been tested on various real- world situations.

fields.value: The paper tests passive selection from hand-waving and active attention-based selection during natural dialogue with multiple people; service robots were also tested serving drinks at public events.

quotes.text: The passive method is designed for the robot to recognize common hand-waving gesture, where a Bayessian ensemble approach is proposed to fuse hand detections from depth segmentation, palm shape, skin color, and body pose.
The active method is developed for the robot to perform natural interaction with multiple persons.
The proposed method has been deployed on six robot butlers to serve drinks in open public events.

fields.value: Attention-based addressee selection; the paper distinguishes passive signal detection from active selection based on subtle human cues.

quotes.text: We classify the methods of addressee detection and selection into two categories, namely, passive and active approaches.
In contrast, for active approaches, the robot is able to select a person as an addressee based on subtle cues that are inferred from the human pose, gaze, and facial expression.

fields.value: The authors describe attention as a quantitative score computed by normalizing and integrating visual clues, with larger clue values indicating higher probability that a person is attending to the robot for natural interaction.

quotes.text: Next, a novel algorithm to integrate such rich visual clues to provide a quantitative score of human attention is proposed.

Now, all the extracted visual clues are normalized into [0, 1] except f8 which is within [-1, +1], and the larger the visual clue value is, the higher the probability of the attention from the observed person to the robot for a natural interaction.

fields.value: The attention estimate guides selection of the person the robot should address, supporting engagement management and natural dialogue in multiparty interaction.

quotes.text: This attention score is used to guide the robot to select the most probably person to interact with.
For active methods, the robot must be able to perceive the engagement status of multiple persons and select a person as the addressee to perform the interaction.

fields.value: In the described examples, the robot turned toward the person whose attention level became highest, greeted a person showing smiling and speaking cues, and the attention score dropped when that person turned away to speak with someone else.

fields.value: The active system estimates each person's attention using stereo multi-person detection and tracking, body pose, face and gaze detection, lip motion, and facial expression, combining normalized visual clues through weighted sum or a learned model. fields.value: The paper presents passive hand-wave recognition and active attention-based addressee selection for robots interacting with multiple people. In examples, the robot used visual cues such as position, body pose, gaze, facial expression, and speaking to select and face a person; reported hand-wave fusion detection was 91%.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ3; RQ4; RQ5 — The paper characterizes attention as integrated visual evidence and uses it to select an addressee, reports example interaction outcomes, and describes the vision system and robot platforms. It gives no detail on embodiment's influence.
